info.title: OpenAsy Audit API
info.summary: Known vulnerabilities in the dependencies of every project; a pull request fails only for what it adds.
info.description:
Every screen of audit uses this API, and so can your scripts and CI (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Send `osv-scanner` JSON, or SARIF 2.1.0 from Trivy or Grype, with `AUDIT_INGEST_TOKEN`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description:
Takes the JSON of `osv-scanner --format json`, or a SARIF 2.1.0 log from Trivy, Grype or osv-scanner, and compares it with the default branch. Scans of the default branch become the baseline and the package inventory; every other scan reports only the advisories the baseline does not have and nobody has decided about, and `blocking` counts those at or above the project's `failOn`. The project is created by its first scan.

From osv-scanner's JSON audit reads `results[].source.path`, `results[].packages[].package` (`name`, `version`, `ecosystem`) and for each of `packages[].vulnerabilities[]`: `id`, `aliases`, `summary` (or `details`), `severity[]` (a CVSS v3 vector or a number), `database_specific.severity` and `affected[].ranges[].events[].fixed`. Severity is the CVSS v3 base score when there is one, then the database's label, then medium. A result without a package name is left out.

```bash
osv-scanner --format json --lockfile package-lock.json > osv.json
curl -sf -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_INGEST_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @osv.json \
  "https://audit.example.com/api/v1/scans?project=acme/web&branch=$BRANCH&commit=$SHA&pullRequest=$PR" | tee scan.json
test "$(jq .passed scan.json)" = true
```

osv-scanner lists the packages that have advisories unless it is asked for all of them; the inventory holds what the report lists. The body may be gzipped (`Content-Encoding: gzip`), up to 64 MiB unpacked, with at most 50,000 advisories.

Takes AUDIT_INGEST_TOKEN, or an API token with the editor role.

parameters.name: pullRequest
parameters.description: The pull request number or name. A scan of the default branch with a pull request is still compared, not made the baseline.

parameters.name: defaultBranch
parameters.description: Set when the project is new or the default branch changed. Without it a new project uses `main`.

schema.description: The JSON of `osv-scanner --format json` (a `results` array) or a SARIF 2.1.0 log (a `runs` array).

201.description: Compared with the baseline. `passed` says whether the check passes.

200.description: The scan and the advisories it added.

patch.description:
Sets the default branch whose scans are the baseline, and the severity that fails a check.

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Deletes its scans, advisories, inventory and decisions.

Needs the admin role.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (default): reported on the default branch and not decided about. `suppressed`: decided about and still reported. `resolved`: no longer reported, usually because the dependency was updated.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the advisory, its aliases (CVE ids), the package or the summary.

put.description:
Marks an advisory as a false positive, not affecting you (the vulnerable code is not used) or accepted risk, with a reason, or opens it again. The decision follows the fingerprint to every branch, so a pull request that adds the same advisory does not fail. An advisory that is only in a pull request can be decided about too.

Needs the editor role.

parameters.description: From a finding or a scan.

get.description:
Searches the inventory of the default branch of every project: which projects use a package, in which version and lockfile.

Needs the viewer role.

parameters.description: A part of the package name.

200.description: Packages on the default branches, by name.

Metrics in the Prometheus text format.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when audit runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the audit origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_audit_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when audit is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `AUDIT_INGEST_TOKEN`: for CI. It can send scans, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

FailOn.description: The lowest severity of a new finding that fails the check; `none` never fails it.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

suppressed.description: Open advisories someone has decided about.

fixable.description: Open advisories with a fixed version.

failingChecks.description: Scans of the last 7 days that failed their check.

packages.description: Distinct package versions on the default branch.

nextCursor.description: Pass the previous page's nextCursor to get the next page.

active.description: False once the acceptance has expired; the advisory is open again.

state.description: `not-affected`: the vulnerable code is not used. `open` clears an earlier decision.

reason.description: Required for every state but open.

expiresAt.description: Required for accepted, at most 366 days away; optional for the others.

fingerprint.description: The same on every branch: ecosystem, package, version and advisory.

ecosystem.description: As OSV names it: npm, PyPI, Go, crates.io, Packagist.

advisory.description: The advisory's own id, such as GHSA-... or CVE-...

path.description: The lockfile or manifest it was found in.
